items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember he used to come home sometimes, and he was always whistling this song... It was Jumpin’ with Symphony Sid, Lester Young.

ctx.x: It seems that music was emphasized in the house, since you said everyone had piano lessons. What were your parents listening to? What music did they play in the house, if at all?

That’s interesting. My mother used to watch t.v. She’d watch Lawrence Welk. She loved Lawrence Welk. I think my father – he never went out that much to listen to music. But he – I remember he used to come home sometimes, and he was always whistling this song. It used to drive me crazy until I moved to New York and discovered what it was. It was Jumpin’ with Symphony Sid, Lester Young. He was always whistling
that song. Like I say, he didn’t go out and hang out and listen, but I think he appreciated the music.
